Set reminders for key application windows so you don’t miss new openings for 2025-2026. Are you searching for the best way to study in Europe without worrying about tuition or living costs? Fully funded scholarships in the Netherlands for international students 2025-2026 open doors to top universities and programs at no personal expense. These scholarships offer a chance for you to get a quality education, make global connections, and experience life in one of Europe’s safest and most innovative countries. If you want to earn a degree while all major costs are covered, this guide to fully funded scholarships in the Netherlands is for you. 1) Holland Scholarship for non-EEA international students The Holland Scholarship is designed for international students from outside the European Economic Area (EEA) who want to study for a bachelor’s or master’s degree in the Netherlands. This award stands out for its strong support of students from across the world. You can use the Holland Scholarship at many top Dutch research universities and universities of applied sciences. These schools are located in cities such as Amsterdam, Delft, Groningen, and Rotterdam. The program is meant for talented students seeking new academic and cultural experiences. The scholarship provides a €5,000 grant for your first year of studies . This money helps cover living costs, books, or other expenses after you arrive. The award is a one-time grant and is not renewable for following years. Here is a data-rich summary of the key details: Feature Details Award type €5,000 one-time grant Target group Non-EEA international students Degree levels Bachelor’s and Master’s Eligible fields All fields at participating Dutch universities Number of awards Over 1,500 per year Application period November 2025 – February 2026 (varies by institution) Use First academic year only Renewability Not renewable To apply, you must be from a country outside the EEA and meet the requirements of your chosen Dutch university. Check each university’s application deadline and process for the Holland Scholarship because dates and details differ by institution. Learn more about program details, eligibility, and participating universities by visiting the official Annual Report 2020 or your destination university’s scholarship office. 2) Orange Knowledge Programme (OKP) The Orange Knowledge Programme (OKP) is a fully funded scholarship from the Dutch government for international professionals. Its most distinctive feature is the broad range of short courses and master’s programs offered at top universities across the Netherlands. You can study in various cities, including Amsterdam, Rotterdam, and Utrecht. The Netherlands is well known for its welcoming environment and diverse, multicultural settings. OKP targets mid-career professionals from selected countries who want to strengthen their skills and return to support development in their home countries. Award Details for 2025-2026: Feature Details Type Fully funded Who can apply Professionals from eligible countries (middle income and low income) Academic levels Short courses, Master’s Funding covers Tuition, living expenses, visa, travel, insurance Number of awards Varies, hundreds each year Duration Short courses (2 weeks–12 months); Masters (12–24 months) Fields covered Water, food security, gender, health, and more Application cycles 2–3 rounds yearly; next round for 2025 opens mid-year You must work in a sector or organization that is relevant for your country’s development. The scholarship does not cover undergraduate study. Selection is competitive, with preference for applicants who show commitment to using their new skills for positive impact at home. Most applicants need employer support when applying. You will need an official nomination or reference letter from your workplace. Always check the specific deadlines and eligible countries each year. Some fields are prioritized, so review current announcements before you apply. 3) Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship The Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship is a fully funded scholarship for talented international students who wish to study in the Netherlands . Maastricht University is located in Maastricht , a lively city in the south of the Netherlands. This program is known for its support of bright minds from outside the EU/EEA who want to join one of the top Dutch research universities. You can apply for this scholarship if you are planning to start a master’s program at Maastricht University in the 2025-2026 academic year. The scholarship aims to help outstanding students who have excellent academic records and who would not be able to study in the Netherlands without financial support . Detailed Scholarship Information: Category Description Award type Fully funded (tuition + living costs) Number of awards/year About 24 Academic level Master’s degree Duration 13–24 months (full program duration) Target group Non-EU/EEA international students Coverage Tuition fees, €12,350–€23,750 living stipend, health insurance, visa costs Application window November 2025 – February 2026 (for 2026-2027 programs) Key features and benefits: You receive a full tuition waiver plus a generous monthly stipend for housing and expenses. The scholarship also covers your health and liability insurance and your visa application costs . All master’s programs in English are eligible. Selection is based on academic merit, potential for leadership, and your motivation letter. Application opens each year, so you can check program deadlines for future cycles. You must have been admitted to a Maastricht master’s program to be eligible. This opportunity gives you access to innovative teaching in an international setting, with a strong focus on small-group learning and real-world skills. 4) HAN University NL Scholarship €12,500 HAN University of Applied Sciences in Arnhem and Nijmegen, Netherlands, offers the NL Scholarship valued at €12,500 for new international students in 2025–2026. The scholarship supports talented non-EEA students applying for bachelor’s or master’s programs at HAN. Both campuses are located in friendly cities with strong links to technology, healthcare, and business employers—giving you access to real-world career opportunities during and after your studies. You can apply if you hold a non-EEA passport and have good academic results. The scholarship is awarded for the first year of your study and is based on your grades and motivation letter. Key Facts: Criteria Details Scholarship Type Tuition reduction Value €12,500 (up to 1st year) Number of Awards Limited, competitive Eligible Degrees Bachelor’s and Master’s Target Audience Non-EEA international students Application Period Open now, deadlines vary Selection Basis Academic merit + motivation You will use the funding mainly for tuition fees. The application process is straightforward: apply for a HAN degree program, submit your documents, and write a clear, strong motivation letter. Benefits include studying in a welcoming, international environment, career networking events, and access to internships in Dutch companies. Check upcoming deadlines and eligibility on HAN’s website to start your scholarship application for a rewarding academic experience in the Netherlands. 5) Radboud Scholarship Programme The Radboud Scholarship Programme is a fully funded opportunity offered by Radboud University, one of the largest research universities in the Netherlands. Radboud University is located in Nijmegen, a student-friendly city known for its historic charm and innovative academic environment. This scholarship is designed for non-EEA (European Economic Area) students applying for English-taught master’s degree programs at Radboud University. It rewards academic excellence and seeks future leaders from around the world. Scholarship Details for 2025-2026: Type: Fully funded Coverage: Tuition fees, residence permit costs, insurance, and partial living expenses Number available for the NL scholarship program varies each year. Multiple per year, varies by faculty and program Eligibility: Outstanding non-EEA students, applying for a full-time master’s starting in 2025 or 2026 Duration: Full length of the master’s program (typically 2 years) Field of study: Wide range, including Science, Arts, Social Sciences, Law, Philosophy, Medical Sciences, and more Key features include: You receive a fee waiver which reduces the tuition to that of a Dutch student. The scholarship also provides additional funding to help with living expenses, making it a strong fully funded package. Radboud University is known for its inclusive campus culture and high-quality education. Research and teaching go hand-in-hand, giving you access to modern labs and real-world projects. Learn more about life at Radboud in Nijmegen from the Radboud University overview . Application for the 2025 intake opens late 2024. Always check faculty-specific deadlines, as they may vary by program. Selection is highly competitive and based on academic record, motivation, and potential for impact in your field. The Radboud Scholarship Programme is one of the most sought-after fully funded scholarships for international students in the Netherlands to pursue a master’s. 6) Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degrees Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degrees (EMJMDs) offer fully funded scholarships for international students from any country. This program is popular because it lets you study in at least two different European countries, including the Netherlands, and earn a joint or double degree.
